title: God's Justice Comes to Jerusalem
english: Tomos 5. The vision of the valley of Zion.

Having foretold the capture of the Egyptians, the Assyrians, and the Idumeans, the prophet comes to the holy city itself, that is, Jerusalem, and usefully foretells what would befall it from time to time through divine wrath. He does this so that they might know that the God of all is the ruler of justice, or rather is justice itself. He does not honour, welcome, and care for someone simply because that person has become his own by being schooled under the law; rather, he tests what each has lived, and grants good things to those whose way of life is good, but counts the lover of wickedness a stranger and in no way his own, even if such a person should happen to be beloved for the sake of the fathers (Romans 11:28).

Out of very great ignorance, the Jewish people thought that they would be wholly beyond the reach of their enemies, and that, with no one at all attacking them, they would live out a quiet life in great prosperity, even though they were offending God and had sunk into very great ungodliness. For they worshipped idols, and setting up images and altars under oak and poplar (Hosea 4:13), they offered sacrifices and poured libations to vain things, utterly disregarding the glory owed to the all-holy God.

So through the voice of Jeremiah he says to them about Jerusalem: “And do not say, ‘It is the temple of the Lord’; for unless you thoroughly amend your ways and your practices, I will make this house like Shiloh” (Jeremiah 7:4–5; 26:6).

Again he accused them through the prophet Micah, saying: “Her rulers judged for bribes, and her priests answered for hire, and her prophets divined for silver; and they leaned on the Lord, saying, ‘Is not the Lord among us? No evil will come upon us.’ Therefore, because of you, Zion will be ploughed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a hut for guarding fruit, and the mountain of the house like a grove in a thicket” (Micah 3:11–12).

And the inspired John also made it plain to them that God's judgment comes swiftly upon everyone who makes a habit of wrongdoing, when he said: “Brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bear fruits, then, worthy of repentance, and do not presume to say within yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father’; for I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham” (Matthew 3:7–9). “Even now…” (Matthew 3:10)
